security_audit.summary: Most static external-command detections are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and instructional code fences. I found real local filesystem risks in the initializer and packager: path traversal during skill creation and unintended file inclusion during archive creation.

remediation.issue: Unvalidated skill_name can escape the output directory.
remediation.suggestion: Validate skill_name against the documented hyphen-case rule before path construction. Resolve the final path and require it to remain under the chosen output directory.

remediation.issue: Packaging recursively archives all files under the skill path.
remediation.suggestion: Skip symlinks and verify each resolved file remains inside the skill root before calling zipf.write. Warn before packaging hidden files or secrets.

remediation.issue: Skill instructions ask agents to run helper scripts without trust guidance.
remediation.suggestion: State that scripts should run only on trusted local paths. Review generated files before packaging or sharing them.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Skill Name Path Traversal
semantic_findings.description: The initializer reads the skill name from command arguments and appends it to the output path before creating directories and files. A name containing path separators or dot segments could create files outside the intended directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code documents hyphen-case requirements but does not enforce them before constructing skill_dir and calling mkdir. The write operations then create SKILL.md and resource files under that path.

semantic_findings.title: Potential Symlink Disclosure During Packaging
semantic_findings.description: The packager recursively adds every file under the skill path to a zip without rejecting symlinks or verifying resolved paths stay inside the skill directory. A crafted skill tree could include local files outside the skill package.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Path.rglob plus is_file can treat symlinks to files as packageable inputs, and zipf.write reads the target content. This is a plausible local disclosure risk, but exploitation depends on crafted symlinks.

content.value_statement: Creating reusable AI skills is hard when structure, resources, and packaging rules are unclear. This skill provides a practical workflow for planning, writing, validating, and packaging skills.
actual_capabilities: Explains required SKILL.md frontmatter and metadata quality rules.
Helps choose scripts, references, and assets for reusable workflows.
Guides concrete examples into workflow-based or task-based skill structure.
Provides an initializer script that creates a template skill directory.
Provides validation and packaging scripts for local zip distribution.
Describes an iteration workflow for improving skills after real use.
limitations: It does not replace manual review of generated skill instructions.
Bundled scripts write files and require trusted local paths.
Validation checks basic structure, not full security or policy quality.
It does not publish skills to a marketplace.

use_cases.title: Create a New Internal Skill
use_cases.description: Plan a new skill from user examples, then generate a clear structure and reusable resources.

use_cases.title: Package a Reusable Workflow
use_cases.description: Turn repeated document, data, or automation work into a skill with scripts and references.

use_cases.title: Improve an Existing Skill
use_cases.description: Review a working skill, remove weak examples, improve SKILL.md, and prepare a distributable package.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Simple Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a new skill for [task]. Ask only the key questions needed to define the first version.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Reusable Resources
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate design for scripts, references, and assets.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these example user requests for my skill. Recommend which scripts, references, and assets should be included.

prompt_templates.title: Draft the Skill Instructions
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a SKILL.md outline for this skill. Use clear trigger guidance, workflow steps, and resource references.

prompt_templates.title: Refine and Package a Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this existing skill for clarity, resource fit, validation readiness, and packaging risks before distribution.

output_examples.input: I need a skill that helps rotate and combine PDF files.
output_examples.output: A proposed skill plan with trigger examples, a PDF workflow section, helper script recommendations, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Our team repeats the same customer onboarding checklist every week.
output_examples.output: A task-based skill structure with checklist references, reusable templates, and guidance for updating the workflow after use.

output_examples.input: Check whether my draft skill is ready to package.
output_examples.output: A review summary covering metadata, missing resources, unclear instructions, validation readiness, and packaging cautions.

best_practices: Start from concrete user requests before choosing the skill structure.
Keep SKILL.md concise and move detailed material into references.
Delete unused example files before packaging a skill.
anti_patterns: Do not create a broad skill without clear trigger scenarios.
Do not duplicate the same information across SKILL.md and references.
Do not package placeholder scripts or assets that the skill does not use.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create AI skills with clear instructions, reusable resources, validation steps, and packaging guidance.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it generate starter files?
faq.answer: Yes. The included initializer can create a template skill directory with example resource folders.

faq.question: Does it validate security issues?
faq.answer: No. Its validator checks basic skill structure and metadata, not a full security review.

faq.question: When should references be used?
faq.answer: Use references for detailed documentation, schemas, policies, or workflows that are too large for SKILL.md.

faq.question: What should be removed before packaging?
faq.answer: Remove unused placeholders, example files, stale assets, and any local files that should not be distributed.
